diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows \cite[Lemma 2.4]{dwivedi2024numerical} and adapts it to the two-dimensional setting.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed pointwise inequality is false already for alpha=2 (the classical Laplacian): on the torus take x_2-independent f=cos x_1, g=cos 2x_1; then -Delta(fg)=1/2(cos x_1+9 cos 3x_1) equals 2*sqrt(2)>0 at x_1=3pi/4, while f(-Delta)g+g(-Delta)f=5 cos x_1 cos 2x_1=0 there, so no constant C(alpha) can work (the exact identity -Delta(fg)=f(-Delta)g+g(-Delta)f-2 grad f . grad g has a sign-indefinite correction term). The norm consequence (product_estimate_norm) is a true Kato-Ponce-type estimate, but it cannot be deduced from the false pointwise claim, and the proof field contains only an adaptation assertion for a 1D result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the pointwise claim and state and prove (or correctly cite, in this exact 2D periodic fractional setting) the standard L^2-L^\infty fractional Leibniz/Kato-Ponce estimate, which is the only part used downstream.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 2.2 as stated is false and unproved; the fractional product estimate invoked later in (est_nonl) is supported only after the lemma is restated in its (true) norm form with a valid proof or citation.
issues.title: False pointwise fractional Leibniz (product) inequality in Lemma 2.2
issues.why_classification: The repair requires excising a false statement and supplying a nontrivial known estimate with a valid proof or citation; once replaced, every later use (which needs only the norm form) stands unchanged, so the loss is contained but more than routine.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for all $t\leq\bar T$, where the constant $C = C(\norm{u_0}_{1+\alpha}, \alpha, \bar T)$ is independent of $N$.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound (bd3) is proved only on [0,\bar T], with \bar T = 1/(C ||u_0||_{1+alpha}) determined by the current H^{1+alpha} norm; the remark's premise 'bounded ... uniformly in time (bd3)' is precisely what is not known. On each restart the norm may double (D <= 4 D_0), so the step lengths shrink geometrically (\bar T_k = \bar T_0 / 2^k) and the iteration accumulates at most 2\bar T_0, never reaching arbitrary T. The conserved mass, momentum, and Hamiltonian control at most the H^{alpha/2} norm, and the paper's own comparison solution e(t) blows up in finite time, so no global H^{1+alpha} bound is available from the source's tools. Theorem 3.2's 'for all T >= 0' therefore remains unproved; the argument establishes only local existence and uniqueness on [0,\bar T].

failure_location.quote: Since the semi-discrete approximation is bounded on the $H^{1+\alpha}_{\mathrm{per}}$-norm uniformly in time \eqref{bd3}, we may repeatedly apply the local existence and uniqueness Lemma \ref{conv_lemma}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken Theorem 3.2 (and correspondingly the time range of Theorem 4.3 and of the fully discrete estimates) to the local interval [0,\bar T] furnished by Lemma (conv_lemma); a global statement would require a genuinely new global a priori H^{1+alpha} bound that the present conservation laws and estimates cannot provide.
issues.overall_effect: Global existence and uniqueness for the fZK equation (Theorem 3.2) is unsupported; only a local result is proved. The spectral error estimate of Theorem 4.3, whose proof invokes (bd3) on the whole interval [0,T], is likewise valid only on [0,\bar T], as are the fully discrete error claims of Section 5 and the global convergence claims in the abstract and introduction.
issues.title: Global-in-time existence/uniqueness unsupported: the iterative continuation in Remark 3.3 is invalid
issues.why_classification: Every source-supported resolution either downgrades a central guarantee from global ('for all T >= 0') to local in time, changing a central quantifier and dragging Theorem 4.3 onto [0,\bar T], or requires a new global estimate that the source's own tools (a finite-time blow-up comparison ODE and H^{alpha/2}-level conservation laws) demonstrably cannot supply.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and Sobolev embedding $H^{1+\alpha}(\Omega) \hookrightarrow L^\infty(\Omega)$:

issues.failure_explanation: Closing (est_nonl) requires ||\partial_{x_1} u_N||_{L^\infty} <= C ||u_N||_{1+alpha}, i.e. H^{1+alpha} hookrightarrow W^{1,\infty}; in two dimensions this embedding holds exactly for alpha>1 and fails at alpha=1 (H^2 hookrightarrow L^\infty but grad u in H^1 does not embed into L^\infty: critical logarithmic divergence), and the inverse inequality only gives a growing factor N. The same failing embedding is used to bound ||\partial_{x_1}(\bar u + \bar w)||_{L^\infty} in the uniqueness argument. Hence for alpha=1 the uniform bound (bd3), the convergence, and the uniqueness are not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the hypotheses to alpha in (1,2] (or assume extra regularity at alpha=1); recovering the endpoint with N-uniform bounds would require a different argument, since the natural refinement (Brezis-Wainger-type logarithmic loss) destroys N-uniformity.
issues.overall_effect: All results stated for alpha in [1,2] lose the endpoint alpha=1 (the Benjamin-Ono-type case highlighted in the introduction): local well-posedness, convergence of the scheme, and the error estimates are unproved there.
issues.title: Critical 2D Sobolev embedding used at the endpoint alpha=1 in the H^{1+alpha} a priori estimate and uniqueness argument
issues.why_classification: The least repair is a hypothesis restriction to alpha>1, which preserves a recognizably comparable theory on the open interval but excludes an advertised boundary regime; no short local fix recovers alpha=1.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For brevity and to maintain focus on the novel aspects of our spectral discretization for the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK}, we omit the detailed proofs and refer readers to \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the complete methodology.

issues.failure_explanation: Both projection results that underpin the entire error analysis are unproved; the cited theorem treats the one-dimensional fifth-order Kawahara equation (a different, integer-order operator), and the text only asserts that 'the core analytical techniques remain applicable' without carrying out the required 2D fractional adaptation (higher-norm coercivity of the modified-projection operator and the duality argument). The single derivation actually given, for (proj_erro2), uses |w|_r <= C r! ||w||, which is false even for entire functions (w = e^{i M x_1} gives |w|_r / ||w|| = M^r, unbounded in M), so the exponential estimate is not derived either.

failure_location.quote: The proofs of Theorem \ref{thm:proj_error} and Lemma \ref{lem:time_error} follow the approach developed by Deng \cite[Theorem 2.1]{deng2017optimal} for the Kawahara equation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply complete proofs of Theorem 4.2 and Lemma 4.1 for the fractional 2D operator (or a valid citation for exactly this setting), and derive (proj_erro2) from exponential decay of the Fourier coefficients of analytic functions rather than from the false factorial bound.
issues.overall_effect: The optimal L^2 error estimate and the exponential convergence claim of Theorem 4.3 rest on projection bounds that are not established in the paper.
issues.title: Central projection error estimates (Theorem 4.2 and Lemma 4.1) stated without proof; the one supplied argument contains a false inequality
issues.why_classification: The statements are standard and plausible, so no major loss is expected, but the repair requires a contained nontrivial argument (the adapted coercivity/duality proofs), not a routine fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $u$ be the exact solution of the fZK equation \eqref{eqn:fZK} with initial data $u_0 \in H_{\mathrm{per}}^{r}(\Omega)$, $r \geq \alpha + 5$,
where the constant $C$ depends on $\|u_0\|_{r}$, $\alpha$, and the final time $T$, but is independent of $\Delta t$ and $N$.

issues.failure_explanation: The O(\Delta t^5) remainder involves d^5V/dt^5 with V = e^{-Lt} U; differentiating F(t,V) = e^{-Lt} N(e^{Lt} V) pulls down powers of the diagonal symbol L_m = -i m_1 |m|^alpha (of size up to N^{1+alpha}) — e.g. \partial_t^4 F contains the term L^4 N(U), whose l^2 norm costs roughly 4alpha+5 spatial derivatives. With only r >= alpha+5 the Taylor remainder a priori grows with N; the asserted N-independent constant is an unsupported final sentence, and the stated regularity is insufficient for the standard remainder bound that the proof itself sets up.

failure_location.quote: Under the regularity assumption, the constant in the $\mathcal{O}(\Delta t^5)$ term is bounded uniformly in $N$, completing the proof of the local error estimate.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the regularity hypothesis (e.g. r >= 4alpha+5, enough to control d^5V/dt^5 in l^2 uniformly in N) or provide a structure-based (commutator) argument proving N-uniformity under the stated regularity.
issues.overall_effect: The local (and hence the advertised global O(\Delta t^4)) temporal error bound with an N-independent constant is not established under the stated hypotheses; the combined fully discrete estimate ||u(t_n) - u_N^n|| <= C_1 N^{-r} + C_2 \Delta t^4 inherits this gap.
issues.title: Uniform-in-N truncation-error constant asserted without justification; the stated regularity r >= alpha+5 is insufficient
issues.why_classification: A limited strengthening of the regularity hypothesis salvages the same \Delta t^5 / \Delta t^4 rates, so there is no major loss, but the missing uniformity argument is nontrivial.
